lessons: Focus heavily on Vikram-Betal and detective categories, as they pulled the highest view counts and engagement (e.g., Betal videos reached up to 6 views and 9.8% watch time).
Keep compilation and long-form videos under strict quality control, as 90+ minute compilations currently struggle with near-zero watch retention.
Maintain high-pacing and intrigue in the first 30 seconds since retention drops quickly if the hook is slow.
Rely on classic recurring characters like Gopal Bhar and Betal who maintain baseline audience curiosity.
Avoid overly niche or slow-paced mythological and educational entries until core storytelling pacing improves.
titles: Titles featuring direct questions or urgent mysteries (e.g., 'কে ছড়াল বাগানে উল্টো পায়ের ছাপ?' or 'শ্মশান রাতে বেতালের অদ্ভুত গল্প') generate stronger initial curiosity.
Adding emojis that visually match the core mystery (footprints, skulls, crowns) improves click-through readability in feeds.
Swapped titles generally performed better when they emphasized a character's clever action or an impending threat rather than generic summaries.
requests: More quiz-based interactive segments where viewers guess outcomes in the comments
Character name shoutouts in upcoming episodes based on comment participation
Viewer-voted storylines where the audience decides the next plot direction
More spooky or ghostly elements integrated into detective and mystery formats
More magical objects like the 'jadu pencil' or hidden treasures in fairy-tale settings
